advice: Experiment: change the K-major packing block `Llibxsmm_78` so it packs one 32-row Aᵀ panel at a time into a 64 KiB scratch area, then update the matching scratch base and stride in the two consumers `Llibxsmm_478` and `Llibxsmm_70c`. Keep each packed panel live while the existing 32-column B panels consume it; advance to the next 32-row panel only after its outputs are complete. The current pack loop fills 64 rows (128 KiB), and the consumers address those halves at offsets 0 and 65536 bytes. This tests whether reducing the packed working set changes performance; cache pressure is only a hypothesis, not established by the supplied cache sizes or scores.
risks: This changes packing lifetime, scratch addressing, and the traversal needed to finish each row panel. A bad base, stride, or loop order can overwrite scratch early, omit or duplicate C tiles, or read beyond the panel. Preserve the fixed GEMM ABI, FP32 operation and tolerance, general-size fallback, packing inside `gemm`, balanced SME state transitions, and complete BSD-3-Clause notice. Check assembler and ABI correctness, output coverage, n=512, general sizes with odd tails, and n<=0. Then use fresh repeated paired controls under unchanged benchmark and power conditions, report spread, and apply the existing promotion rules. Do not infer a cache bottleneck or causal gain from noisy scores.
